title: AI-guided polyVERSE discovery yields a high-temperature dielectric polymer with 8.3 J cm⁻³ energy density
summary: The polyVERSE workflow used reaction-aware polymer generation and machine-learning property screens to identify PONB-2Me5Cl, which the researchers synthesized and cast into films. Experimental characterization measured a discharged energy density of 8.3 J cm⁻³ at 200 °C and a breakdown field of 750 MV m⁻¹; the paper compares this energy density with commercial polymer dielectrics at the same temperature. This is a laboratory polymer-film result, not a packaged capacitor or aerospace-ready device.
ai_technology: polyVERSE with four polymer graph neural-network property predictors
organization: Georgia Institute of Technology and University of Connecticut

evidence.tested: The polyVERSE workflow used reaction-aware polymer generation and machine-learning property screens to identify PONB-2Me5Cl, which the researchers synthesized and cast into films.
evidence.unknown: The reported 8.3 J cm⁻³ is measured on synthesized polymer films under the article’s laboratory breakdown and dielectric characterization protocol. The comparison with commercial polymers is the authors’ reported comparison; the work does not demonstrate a packaged capacitor, operational lifetime, aerospace use, or scale-up. Other suggested polyimides in the paper remain predicted and are not counted here. The reported polymerization used non-green solvents.
evidence.ai_role: polyVERSE generated polymers from commercially available monomers using encoded reaction templates, then machine-learning models predicted glass-transition temperature, band gap and dielectric properties for screening. AI down-selected polymer candidates for synthesis; PONB-2Me5Cl was subsequently synthesized and its dielectric properties were measured.
